chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Let there be a proclamation of war from Me upon the one who hurts My believing servant, and let him be safe from My anger, the one who honors My believing servant.'

And if there were not from My creation in the earth, between the east and the west, except for one believer along with a just Imam, I would have sufficed by their worship from all that I created in My earth, and I would have established the seven skies and the earths due to them both, and would have made for them both a comfort from their faith, so they would not be in need of the comfort of anyone besides themselves.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of a single believer and a just Imam in Islamic theology according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This Hadith Qudsi, recorded in Al-Kafi, underscores the high status of the 'Abd Allah al-Mu'min' (Servant of God who is a believer) by linking their honor directly to divine war and peace. It highlights the cosmological significance of the Just Imam and the believer, suggesting that their worship is sufficient to sustain the heavens and earth, a concept central to Shia theology regarding the role of the Ahl al-Bayt and the faithful in maintaining cosmic order.
